title: Sunny and the Nesting Birds | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka discovers a nest tucked into a low bush — woven from grass and bark and soft threads — and wonders how long the birds worked to make something so round, so perfect, so right. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The nest was tucked into the low bush.

Sunny almost missed it — it was the exact colour of the surrounding twigs and bark, woven in so carefully it seemed to grow from the branch. She only saw it because the moonlight caught the inside of it at just the right angle, and she saw the smoothness there.

She leaned very close without touching.

It was empty now — whatever birds had made it had moved on. But she could see how it was made. Grasses twisted into a firm outer ring. Bark strips woven through for structure. Soft fibres — from spiderwebs, maybe — lining the inside, making it smooth and yielding.

Round. Perfect. Just the right size for something small and precious.

She thought about how long it must have taken. Trip after trip, each beak carrying one piece of grass, one strip of bark, one thread of silk. Days of patient, careful work, each piece placed just so.

All of it so that someone small could sleep safely.

She sat back on her heels and looked at the nest from a little distance.

It was one of the most beautiful things she had ever seen. Not despite its smallness — because of it.

She sat under the bush for a long time.

The empty nest sat above her, holding the shape of the birds that had once slept in it.

She fell asleep below it.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little nest. Goodnight, little one.
